decisions.title: Where the supervisor prototype runs

options.label: Real throwaway plugin service inside a development WednesdayAI gateway installed on this host
options.consequence: Proves plugin loading, registerService lifecycle and recovery after a real gateway restart; costs a one-time gateway install that then serves every later phase.

options.label: Standalone Node script under plugins/shohin/spike/, run with node
options.consequence: Answers the scope, HOME and runner questions with no gateway, but leaves plugin loading and restart ordering as assumptions.

options.label: Bash-only harness
options.consequence: Fast, but the file tailing, heartbeat and identity checks Phase 1 needs are Node concerns; nothing learned would transfer.

decisions.rationale: The operator directed on 2026-09-05 that a development gateway can and should be installed on this host. With it available, the real plugin path costs little more than the script and answers strictly more.

decisions.title: Containment mechanism

options.label: systemd-run --user --scope with RuntimeMaxSec
options.consequence: One cgroup holds every descendant including setsid children; systemctl kill stops all of them; a runtime ceiling is enforced by the OS.

options.label: Detached process group
options.consequence: A child that calls setsid escapes; nothing enforces a ceiling when the supervisor dies.

options.label: Container per run
options.consequence: Strongest, but core's sandbox is optional Docker and this is Phase 8 scope.

decisions.rationale: The user session is running and a scope launch succeeded on this host (A1).

decisions.title: Target topic for the runner

options.label: Separate throwaway topic shohin-spike-target prepared by hand through the WAI flow
options.consequence: The runner's preflights run for real; the topic is deleted at close.

options.label: Run the spike against its own decomposed plan
options.consequence: Circular: the runner would be executing the tasks that build the harness that runs it.

options.label: WAI_DAG_TEST_MODE fixture
options.consequence: Skips freshness and plan lint, which are among the preconditions the spike must inventory.

decisions.rationale: Only a real topic exercises the precheck token, lint and branch requirements SC6 must list.

decisions.title: How the ephemeral HOME is built

options.label: Empty allow-list grown by observed OpenCode failures
options.consequence: Yields the minimal file set with evidence per file; slower by a few iterations.

options.label: Mirror the operator's HOME read-only
options.consequence: Works immediately but exposes every credential and proves nothing about minimality.

decisions.rationale: SC2 requires the list of files and the error seen without each; only the grown list produces that.

decisions.title: Which runner copy to run

options.label: Installed copy under ~/.agents/wai/scripts (sha256 4542740276d8...)
options.consequence: Matches what a plugin on this host would find; the drift from the repo source becomes a recorded finding.

options.label: Repo source under /data/Code/agent-plugins (sha256 3fe1c1c05c58...)
options.consequence: Reviewed code, but not what is deployed; would hide the drift.

decisions.rationale: Phase 1 pins by sha256 whatever is installed; the spike must measure that copy.

decisions.title: Spend and time caps for the spike

options.label: USD 50 per spike day, 30 minutes per attempt, one attempt for the baseline
options.consequence: Cost attributable per rung; a runaway is bounded by the scope ceiling.

options.label: No cap
options.consequence: A stuck ladder could burn the day's budget with nothing learned.

options.label: USD 10
options.consequence: Likely too little for baseline plus attach plus attention runs on the frontier rungs.

decisions.rationale: The constraint names the operator's cap without a value; USD 50 is the recorded default and the operator may override before the run.

decisions.title: How gateway death is exercised

options.label: SIGKILL the openclaw-gateway user unit mid-run and let its Restart= policy bring it back
options.consequence: Observes the real failure and the real restart ordering: scope survives or not, watchdog fires or not, recovery sweep runs on plugin load.

options.label: SIGKILL a standalone supervisor script
options.consequence: Reproduces heartbeat loss only; cannot observe restart ordering or the recovery sweep.

decisions.rationale: D1 puts the supervisor inside the gateway, so the real event is available at no extra cost.

decisions.title: How the worker ladder is passed

options.label: Model ids in WAI_DAG_WORKER_MODELS, unpatched runner
options.consequence: Uses the runner's existing -m path; if a provider is not reachable that way the report says so.

options.label: Patch the spike's runner copy to pass --agent first
options.consequence: Tests a change agent-plugins has not accepted before the unpatched behaviour is known.

decisions.rationale: Measure the shipped path first; patch only on evidence.

decisions.title: Cleanup of throwaway artifacts

options.label: Delete the spike directory, the target topic's plan directory and its branch in a final irreversible task gated by operator approval
options.consequence: SC8 holds; nothing from the spike survives; the deletion needs a human token.

decisions.single_option_reason: SC8 admits no other outcome; the only fork is who approves the deletion, and irreversible tasks always require the operator.

decisions.title: Gateway install method

options.label: Build /data/Code/WednesdayAI-core from source, npm pack, npm install -g the tarball, wednesdayai onboard --install-daemon
options.consequence: Plugin SDK version matches what this repo compiles against; a real systemd user unit exists to kill and observe; install is documented in core AGENTS.md section 8.

options.label: npm install -g wednesdayai@latest (0.4.10)
options.consequence: Fastest, but one version behind the local 0.4.11 source and its plugin-sdk; risks SDK mismatch findings that are not about the spike.

options.label: pnpm gateway:dev in the core checkout
options.consequence: No systemd unit and no daemon, so gateway death and restart cannot be observed; channels skipped by default is the only advantage and onboard offers the same.

decisions.rationale: The spike needs a real unit to kill and a matching SDK; the source build gives both. The dev gateway persists as host infrastructure by the operator's direction.

obstacles.obstacle: The user session's cgroup delegation does not cover the runner's children, so systemctl kill misses grandchildren.
obstacles.countermeasure: TS1 spawns a deliberate setsid child and lists survivors; if any survive, the report records the fallback (process group plus watchdog) and the residual risk for Phase 1.

obstacles.obstacle: OpenCode reads auth from a location outside HOME (XDG dirs, keyring) so no copy-in list ever suffices.
obstacles.countermeasure: Grow env.allow with XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at the ephemeral HOME; record every variable required alongside every file.

obstacles.obstacle: The runner's -m path cannot express the operator's sub-agent (system prompt, tools) so the model id reaches the provider but not the agent behaviour.
obstacles.countermeasure: Report states this plainly; D8's second option is exercised on the runner copy and its diff recorded as a proposal for agent-plugins.

obstacles.obstacle: opencode serve attach fails or the runner's probe declares cold dispatch.
obstacles.countermeasure: SC3b accepts a recorded failure with cause; the probe captures the runner's warning line.

obstacles.obstacle: The runner never raises attention on the chosen task, so the notify path is untested.
obstacles.countermeasure: TS4 uses a task whose scope test cannot pass; if attention still does not fire, a deterministic gate failure is forced by editing the task's expected output in the worktree.

obstacles.obstacle: The watchdog and RuntimeMaxSec both stop the run, so the report cannot say which mechanism acted.
obstacles.countermeasure: Run the probe twice: once with the ceiling far above the watchdog threshold, once with the watchdog disabled.

obstacles.obstacle: The runner invokes binaries via PATH lookups the log does not show, so the inventory is incomplete.
obstacles.countermeasure: TS6 uses strace -f -e execve for one run, or a PATH shim directory that logs every execution, and reconciles with the log.

obstacles.obstacle: A read-only TMPDIR makes the runner fail before the lane step, so fallback behaviour is never reached.
obstacles.countermeasure: Point TMPDIR at a writable directory and make only the worktree target path unwritable; if the runner has no such split, patch the copy to inject the failure at the lane step and record the patch.

obstacles.obstacle: The report references files that will be deleted, so it becomes unreadable after cleanup.
obstacles.countermeasure: The report embeds evidence inline and names deleted paths as historical; TS8 runs after the report commit.

obstacles.obstacle: Pre-mortem: the spike burned the budget on the frontier rungs before the cheap rung was measured, and the report has cost numbers for one rung only.
obstacles.countermeasure: Baseline runs with WAI_DAG_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1 so only the first rung executes; higher rungs are measured in a second, separately budgeted run.

obstacles.obstacle: Pre-mortem: the ephemeral HOME worked in the spike because the operator's OpenCode session had a cached token the copy-in carried, and Phase 1 will fail on a fresh host.
obstacles.countermeasure: The report names each copied file's role (config versus credential versus cache) and flags cache files as non-transferable.

obstacles.obstacle: Pre-mortem: --reset full destroyed commits the report needed, and the recovery policy was written from memory.
obstacles.countermeasure: TS5 captures git rev-list --all and the plan directory listing before every reset, and the worktree is cloned to a scratch path first.

obstacles.obstacle: The unit's Restart= policy brings the gateway back before the scope has ended, so the recovery sweep sees a live scope and re-attaches, and the report cannot separate 'run outlived supervisor' from 'supervisor came back in time'.
obstacles.countermeasure: TS5 captures journal timestamps of kill, restart, plugin load and sweep; the probe is run twice, once with the unit's restart delayed (RestartSec raised in a drop-in) so the ceiling and watchdog are observed in isolation.

obstacles.obstacle: Installing the dev gateway pulls the operator's provider credentials or channel config into the gateway's own environment, and the spike plugin inherits them into the executor environment by accident.
obstacles.countermeasure: The gateway is onboarded with channels skipped and no provider keys beyond what the runner itself needs; TS6 reads /proc/<pid>/environ of the runner and of one OpenCode child and the report lists every variable present.

decision_points.trigger: The OpenCode harness or the model provider behind a ladder rung is unavailable or rejects the request for the whole attempt window, so a probe task cannot obtain an executor.
The cleanup task (D9) is reached: it deletes the spike directory, the target topic's plan directory and branch, and must not run without the operator's approval token.
The spec is amended during the run (for example a probe order change) so the precheck token no longer matches.

assumptions.claim: A systemd user session is running on this host and `systemd-run --user --scope` can launch a process with RuntimeMaxSec.
OpenCode is installed and on PATH for the operator user.
The installed runner copy differs from the repo source, so the spike must record the sha256 of what it ran.
The three ladder sub-agents resolve to concrete model ids usable with opencode run -m.

The runner honours WAI_DAG_OPENCODE, WAI_DAG_WORKER_MODELS (ordered ladder), WAI_DAG_NOTIFY_CMD (called with topic, id, 'kind: reason'), WAI_DAG_OPENCODE_SERVER (--attach), and refuses to run without a committed precheck token and lint-clean plan unless WAI_DAG_TEST_MODE=1.
